findings.title: Coverage counts trades from unrelated products
findings.description: `raw_counts` filters `tick_trade` only by session timestamps, while `ledger_totals` is filtered to the requested dataset and symbol shape. Because `tick_trade` is shared across products, a coverage report can count another product’s trades as raw rows for this product and report false mismatches. Restrict raw counts to the relevant instrument set while still detecting raw-only rows for that product.

findings.title: Reports caught up when the wanted end is unknown
findings.description: When an entry has a tier and start date but neither a configured end nor an observed dataset edge, `_wanted_end` returns `None` and `_scope` has no wanted range. However, `caught_up` is still called with `wanted=True`; it can return `True` based only on the held sessions, which does not establish completion through an unknown end. In this case, the report should not claim the product is caught up.

findings.title: New database read paths lack a load test
findings.description: These new status and coverage paths perform database-backed reads, including a time-bounded scan of the `tick_trade` hypertable. The added integration tests verify behavior but do not assert latency, throughput, or resource bounds. The testing rules require a realistic, CI-gated load test for network/database paths.
